name: Digital Fortress

profile.reading: This registry row's operator field was corrected from Equinix to Digital Fortress in an earlier pass, after this facility was divested by Equinix to Chirisa Investments in 2019 and rebranded as Digital Fortress Piscataway; Equinix is retained as former_operator per this registry's no deletion policy. Digital Fortress's own current page for this facility, fetched fresh, gives the address 201B Centennial Avenue, Piscataway Township, New Jersey, and describes a 96,500 square foot building comprising 9,700 square feet of built out white space and 14,000 square feet of shell space available for future buildout, with 1.8 megawatts of UPS power capacity in an N+1 configuration, up to 15 kilowatts per cabinet available without significant redesign, and 800 tons of chilled water cooling capacity. The operator's own page lists SOC I and SOC II Type II compliance, supporting PCI and HIPAA frameworks, along with 24 by 7 network operations center monitoring, key card access, slab on grade concrete construction, and a 48 inch raised floor with underfloor leak and smoke detection. Digital Fortress, per trade press coverage on this registry's separate Meadowville, Virginia row, has operated since 1994, growing from nine facilities nationwide as a multi tenant and wholesale data center provider serving enterprises across multiple states including New Jersey, Virginia, Washington, Oregon, Colorado, and Illinois, and is a Chirisa Investments portfolio company. Baxtel and other aggregators independently corroborate this same address and the operator's current Digital Fortress branding at this building. Piscataway Township sits in Middlesex County, New Jersey, within the broader New York and New Jersey data center corridor that also hosts major Equinix, Digital Realty, and CoreSite campuses tracked elsewhere in this registry, drawing colocation demand from proximity to Manhattan financial and media firms at lower New Jersey real estate and power costs. The buildings continued use as a data center facility across two different operators, first Equinix and now Digital Fortress, reflects a broader industry pattern in which purpose built colocation real estate tends to remain in data center use through ownership changes given the high cost and long lead time of new construction relative to acquiring and rebranding an existing facility.

profile.campus: Digital Fortress Meadowville Technology Park campus, Chesterfield County VA (88-100 acres)
profile.reading: Digital Fortress: Richmond occupies a wholesale data center campus at 1401 Meadowville Technology Parkway, Richmond, Virginia, in Chesterfield County's Meadowville Technology Park, equidistant from Ashburn, Virginia's Data Center Alley and Virginia Beach's transatlantic cable landing stations. Digital Fortress's own dedicated wholesale Richmond page, fetched fresh, describes a 242,000 square foot building on a 100 acre private campus, comprising 18,270 square feet of ready built out white space in a single data hall plus 196,625 square feet of shell and core space for future expansion, with 4.2 megawatts of current power capacity scalable to 25 megawatts, designed to Tier III standards with fully redundant N+1 concurrently maintainable mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems, and Gold LEED certification. A May 21, 2021 unveiling article on the Meadowville Technology Park's own site describes an 88 acre campus figure and a 250,000 square foot LEED Gold building, both broadly consistent with the operator's own more precise figures, and states the campus supports up to 100 megawatts of total on-site power capacity, with the initial 4.1 megawatt facility expandable to 25 megawatts within 20 weeks of a customer commitment. That same coverage describes Digital Fortress as operating since 1994, having grown from nine facilities nationwide to include this Richmond site, offering colocation and cloud access services to enterprises across states including Washington, Oregon, Colorado, and Illinois, consistent with this registry's other Digital Fortress rows. The campus includes a private road entrance, a visitor screening building, Class A office space for up to 120 employees, a dedicated loading dock, and redundant fiber connectivity with diverse demarcation points. Digital Fortress is a Chirisa Investments portfolio company.

profile.reading: Digital Fortress Lynnwood, marketed by the operator as its North Seattle data center, sits at 4200 194th Street Southwest, Lynnwood, Washington 98036. Per the operator's own site, fetched fresh, the facility has been operational since 2006, is designed to Tier 3 standards, is carrier neutral with 24 by 7 support, and provides 6 megawatts of power capacity, a figure independently corroborated by a third party aggregator, DataCenterMap. Digital Fortress, per trade press coverage on this registry's separate Meadowville, Virginia row, has operated since 1994, growing from nine facilities nationwide as a multi tenant and wholesale data center provider serving enterprises across multiple states including Washington, Oregon, Colorado, Illinois, New Jersey, and Virginia, and is a Chirisa Investments portfolio company. No specific square footage was found published for this Lynnwood building this session despite a fresh attempt, an honest gap; the operator's dedicated Lynnwood facility page on digital-fortress.com continues to return a not found error, so the figures here rest on the operator's broader North Seattle marketing page and independent aggregator corroboration rather than a single dedicated facility page. Lynnwood sits immediately north of Seattle in Snohomish County, Washington, a secondary Pacific Northwest data center market that has drawn colocation investment as an alternative to more expensive downtown Seattle real estate while remaining close enough for low latency access to the same carrier hotel infrastructure, including the Westin Building Exchange, that anchors the region's network connectivity. Digital Fortress's Pacific Northwest presence also includes three Portland and Beaverton, Oregon buildings already on file elsewhere in this registry, acquired from Atmosera in January 2021, giving the company a combined Seattle and Portland metro footprint alongside its East Coast Piscataway and Richmond facilities.

reading:
Digital Fortress was founded in 1994 and is a privately held colocation company concentrated in the Seattle, Washington area, with additional facilities in Portland, Oregon, Chicago, Illinois, and Piscataway, New Jersey. The operator's own site gives an inconsistent facility count, stating eight facilities in one section and nine state-of-the-art colocation facilities in another, both recorded here rather than resolved to one number.

The company names three Seattle-area sites, downtown Seattle, South Seattle/Tukwila, and North Seattle/Lynnwood, plus three numbered Portland, Oregon locations. Its Lynnwood facility is the only one with a specific stated capacity, critical load power in excess of 6 megawatts, with other sites described only in redundancy terms, Tier III 2N, rather than megawatt figures. The company operates its own network as Autonomous System AS3361, with client handoff capacity across multiple 100 gigabit per second links.

The registry here tracks 4 Digital Fortress facilities across two states, Oregon and Virginia. Virginia is notable because it does not appear among the eight or nine markets named on the operator's own site, which lists only Washington, Oregon, Illinois, and New Jersey, a discrepancy worth checking during the facility-level research phase, since it may indicate either an unlisted newer Virginia site or a facility misattributed to Digital Fortress in this registry's source data.
